stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{x^{2} - 4}{x - 2}, & x < 2 \\ kx + m, & 2 \le x \le 3 \\ - x^{2}, & x > 3 \end{cases} \), where k and m are constants. Find the values of k and m for which f is continuous for all real numbers.

answer_key.label: \( k = -13 \) and \( m = 30 \), because the middle branch must equal 4 at \( x = 2 \) and -9 at \( x = 3 \).

worked_solution.text: For \( x < 2 \), \( \frac{x^{2} - 4}{x - 2} = x + 2 \), so the limit from the left at \( x = 2 \) is 4. The middle branch gives \( f(2) = 2k + m \), so \( 2k + m = 4 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: match the branches at the first boundary

worked_solution.text: At \( x = 3 \) the middle branch gives \( f(3) = 3k + m \) and the last branch approaches -9, so \( 3k + m = -9 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: match the branches at the second boundary

worked_solution.text: Subtracting the equations gives \( k = -13 \), and then \( m = 30 \).

options.label: No values of k and m work, because \( \frac{x^{2} - 4}{x - 2} \) is undefined at \( x = 2 \), so f has no limit there.
options.derivation: the first branch is undefined at x = 2, and that was taken to mean its limit there does not exist

options.label: \( k = 1 \) and \( m = 2 \), because the middle branch must equal 4 at \( x = 2 \) and 5 at \( x = 3 \).
options.derivation: at x = 3 the first branch, which applies only for x < 2, used in place of the last branch

options.label: \( k = -5 \) and \( m = 6 \), because the middle branch must equal -4 at \( x = 2 \) and -9 at \( x = 3 \).
options.derivation: at x = 2 the last branch, which applies only for x > 3, used in place of the first branch
